sentences.text: Jabalpur against the applicants.
2. The case of the applicants are that they are businessmen dealing in grains.

In the year 2011 they purchased 765 and 729 quintals paddy from various farmers and for the safety of the purchased goods, they hired a warehouse namely Premchand Warehouse situated at Kandrakheda, Panagar,
District Jabalpur, which belongs to one Dilip Sugani.
They stored the purchased paddy and got the receipts as well.
They were in need of some funds for their business for which they raised loan of Rs.12 Lakhs i.e. Rs.6 Lakhs each from respondent No.1 Bank on the basis of receipts of stored paddy.
The respondent No.1 Bank on due verification has sanctioned a loan of Rs.12 Lacs against the receipts and the paddy stored in the warehouse.
Few blank cheques including the cheque in question bearing no.31056 was kept with the respondent No.1 Bank as a security.
The Bank officials have duly visited the warehouse, verified the storage of paddy and thereafter the loan was sanctioned.
In the year 2012 amount of Rs.68,000/- each was deposited by the applicants towards the repayment of loan.
They could not pay the remaining amount of loan, therefore, their account was categorized as NPA and subsequently Bank started recovery proceedings.

When notices of recovery of loan was received by the applicants, they immediately arranged some funds and visited the Bank for settling the loan wherein they came to know about registration of an FIR under Sections 420, 406/34 of the IPC by the Bank against the owner and manager of the warehouse.
It was further informed that the warehouse owner as well as the manager were arrested and thereafter they were granted bail by this Court with the condition of depositing 50 Lakhs with the Bank.
The said amount has been deposited by them.
The applicants were not knowing what has happened but the balance amount of Rs.9 Lakhs was deposited by them i.e. Rs.4.5 Lakhs each and the entire recovery was closed.
After depositing the amount the Bank has released the warehouse receipt in their favour.
No dues certificate was issued in their favour by the respondent No.1 Bank.
Thereafter, they visited the warehouse and demanded the entire paddy stored in the warehouse from the owner and the manager.
The manager refused to give the paddy stored in the warehouse.
They were shocked to see that the entire paddy was missing from the warehouse, hence, an FIR has been registered against the owner and manager of the warehouse.
Several attempts were made by the applicants to get back paddy or the equivalent amount to the tune of Rs.22 Lakhs but the warehouse owner denied the same.

It was informed that the owner of the warehouse was arrested in Crime No.236/2013 registered at Police Station Panagar, Jabalpur and was granted bail by this Court on 09.07.2013 with a condition on deposition of Rs.50 Lakhs in M.Cr.C. No.8040/2013.
Against the fraudulent act of the owner, the applicants made several complaints to the police, however, no action was taken by the police authority.
Therefore, they filed a complaint case against the owner of the warehouse before the competent court which is pending adjudication.

When all these proceedings were going on respondent No.1 Bank in order to recover the amount has made a complaint under Section 156(3)
of the Cr.P.C. alleging that there were 14 persons including the applicants, who raised loans and have failed to pay the same.

It is also alleged by the Bank that the paddy against which the loan was raised was missing, but the fact remains that the entire loan amount as far as applicants are concerned is being settled by them with the respondent No.1 Bank.
They have deposited the entire amount and no dues certificate has been issued by the bank.
On the other hand, they themselves have registered a complaint case against the owner and manager of the warehouse.
Therefore, the proceedings initiated by the respondent No.1 Bank against them is per se illegal.

It is their case that they are victim to the proceedings as on one hand they have lost the entire paddy which was stored Jaipal Panjwani vs Sher Nagrik Sahkari Bank Ltd. on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3404345/
2 by them in the warehouse and on the other hand they have to repay the entire loan amount to the bank virtually cause double loss to the applicants.

entities.text: Jaipal Panjwani vs Sher Nagrik Sahkari Bank Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no element of offence under Section 420 of the IPC against them because the culpable intention at the time of making the initial promise was absent in the matter.
Had it been a condition that they were having a criminal intention against them from the very beginning, then the matter would have been different.

It is further pointed out that the owner as well as the manager has been acquitted in the criminal case registered by the Bank in Sessions Trial No.626 of 2016 vide judgment of acquittal dated 01.06.2023.

Therefore, once the owner as well as the manager who are the principal accused in the case have been acquitted by the trial court, no offence is made out against the present applicants as they are virtually the victims and has faced huge loss.
They themselves have lodged the complaint against the owner and manager when the found paddy missing from the warehouse.
They have prayed for quashment of the entire proceedings.
3. Learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.2/State has supported the registration of the FIR on the ground that the element of criminal conspiracy is available.

The respondent No.2 Bank has registered a complaint against 14 other person including the applicants and by playing conspiracy they got the paddy missing from the warehouse and thereafter loan was taken by them on the receipts which has been issued by the warehouse owner.
Under these circumstances, their involvement is clearly reflected.
The grounds raised are the matter of evidence, therefore, no interference is called for.
They have prayed for dismissal of the petition.

4. Heard learned counsels for the parties and perused the record.
5.
The record indicates that the applicants are the businessmen, who have stored the paddy in the warehouse.
They got the receipts towards storing in the warehouse.
Based on the receipts, they had taken a loan from the respondent No.1 Bank amounting to Rs.12 Lakhs.
The entire record indicates that the loan amount has been repaid by them to the respondent No.1 Bank and no due certificate has been given by the Bank.
The details of repayment of loan has not been disputed as NOCs have been issued by the Bank and the warehouse receipts have been released to them.
When they went to the warehouse to collect the paddy, the same was refused by the manager of the warehouse and thereafter they came to know about the registration of the FIR.
They also registered a complaint against the owner and the warehouse manager.
The record further indicates that the warehouse manager and the owner were granted bail by this court on the condition that on deposition of Rs.50 Lakhs they will be enlarged on bail.
The aforesaid order was complied with.
Eventually, in Sessions Trial No.626/2016 the manager as well as owner were tried which resulted into their acquittal vide judgment of acquittal dated 01.06.2023.
It appears that the applicants being the businessmen, who have kept the paddy in the warehouse were the victim to the proceedings.
On the one hand they have lost all the paddy stored in the warehouse and on the other hand they have to repay the loan amount under compulsion.
The offence which has been registered against them is under Section 420 of the IPC.
The ingredients of Section 420 of the IPC is not available in the present case as the guilty intention from the very inception is not available.

This Court took note of the aforesaid aspect of the matter and vide order 12.02.2018 has granted interim relief in their favour staying the further proceedings pending before the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Jabalpur as far as applicants are concerned.

3 issuance of NOC by the respondent No.1 Bank against the repayment of the loan as well as the release of the receipts.

6. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Vesa Holdings Private Limited and another vs. State of Kerala and others reported in (2015) 8 SCC 293 has considered the similar aspect and has held as under:-
"10.

entities.text: Vesa Holdings Private Limited and another vs. State of Kerala and others reported in (2015) 8 SCC 293
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: We have been taken through the complaint petition in its entirety.

The letter dated 6-8-2008 contains the offer of the appellants as well as the acceptance made by the third respondent, and it reads thus:
"6-8-2008 Mr K.G.S. Nair Keezhoot, Changanasserry Kerala.
Dear Sir, Sub : Settlement of IIBI dues at Rs 8.25 crores.
Please refer to the discussion we had on the above subject.

As discussed we are agreeable to pay you a lump sum amount of Rs 75 lakhs towards consultancy fee for the above settlement,
out of this amount Rs 5 lakhs will be paid upfront for out of pocket expenses and the balance amount Rs 70 lakhs will be paid on completion of the assignment.

We enclose herewith a cheque bearing number 47025 for Rs 30,00,000 (thirty lakhs only) dated 6-8-2008 drawn on HDFC Bank Ltd., which as agreed, this cheque should be presented to Bank only after obtaining acceptance letter from IIBI on or before 30-10-2008 or otherwise the cheque should be returned to us.
Please note that Company should be informed before presenting the said cheque.
If it is agreeable you may return the duplicate of this letter, duly signed in token of acceptance of the offer.

Thanking you, Yours faithfully, For Vesa Holdings (P) Ltd.
Director I accord my consent to this assignment.
(K.G.S. Nair)"
11. It is also not in dispute that IIBI did not issue any acceptance letter on or before 30-10-2008 with regard to the settlement of disputes of the appellant Company.
The third respondent also did not present the cheque dated 6-8-2008 issued by the appellant Company for encashing a sum of Rs 30 lakhs.
Due to the efforts of the appellant Company IIBI finally agreed and issued letter of acceptance dated 5- 1-2009.
One year later, the third respondent sent a letter dated 6-3- 2010 to the appellant Company demanding the balance amount of Rs 70 lakhs towards the consultancy fee.
No allegation whatsoever was made against the appellants herein in the said letter.
It was only mentioned in it that the consultation fee remains unpaid and the Company is delaying the payment on one pretext or the other.
In this context it is relevant to point out that after the expiry of the validity period of the cheque dated 6-8-2008, the third respondent did not ask for reissue of the same.

12. From the decisions cited by the appellant, the settled proposition of law is that every breach of contract would not give rise to an offence of cheating and only in those cases breach of contract would amount to cheating where there was any deception played at the very inception.
If the intention to cheat has developed later on, the same cannot amount to cheating.

In other words for Jaipal Panjwani vs Sher Nagrik Sahkari Bank Ltd. on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3404345/

sentences.text: the purpose of constituting an offence of cheating, the complainant is required to show that the accused had fraudulent or dishonest intention at the time of making promise or representation.

Even in a case where allegations are made in regard to failure on the part of the accused to keep his promise, in the absence of a culpable intention at the time of making initial promise being absent,
no offence under Section 420 of the Penal Code, 1860 can be said to have been made out."
7.
When the element of cheating is absent in the matter no case for registration of FIR is made out.
The case in hand is similar to the aforesaid, which was considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.

From the perusal of the entire facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the Bank has started recovery proceedings towards the loan which has been sanctioned after due verification of the paddy.
At the time of recovery and to ensure that the recovery is done the Bank has got registered a criminal case against the persons to whom they have paid the loan on the ground of criminal conspiracy.
These are virtually civil transactions between the Bank and the borrowers.
The Bank has declared their accounts as NPA, and thereafter, make the complaint.
Even otherwise the applicants have repaid the entire amount and the NOC have been issued by the respondent No.1 Bank along with the receipt of the warehouse.
Under these circumstances, it cannot be said that they were having any guilty intention from the very inception itself.
Therefore, no offence under Sections 406 and 420 of the IPC are made out against the applicants.

The criminal case registered against the applicants who are virtually the victim to the case in hand does not deserve to be continued coupled with the fact that the owner as well as the manager against whom a criminal case has been registered for misappropriating the paddy from the warehouse have been acquitted vide judgment of acquittal dated 01.06.2023.
Under these circumstances, no criminal proceedings can continue against the applicants.
Therefore, the entire criminal proceedings of Complaint Case No.11994 of 2013 pending before the Judicial Magistrate First Class, Jabalpur against the applicants are hereby quashed.
They are discharged from the proceedings.
8. Accordingly, the petition filed under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. stands allowed and disposed off.
9. The order be communicated to the learned trial Court.

(VISHAL MISHRA) JUDGE THK Jaipal Panjwani vs Sher Nagrik Sahkari Bank Ltd. on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3404345/
